title: Package Management
lead: Search, install, update, and remove software with your distribution's package manager; distinguish repositories from the installed package database.
objectives: You know Debian-family systems use apt/dpkg and RHEL-family systems use dnf/rpm.
You can search, inspect, install, update, and remove packages.
You review changes before installation and protect critical packages.

sections.title: Distributions and package tools
body: Package managers download software from signed repositories, resolve dependencies, and update the installed package database. Ubuntu and Debian use `apt` as the high-level tool and `dpkg` for lower-level queries; Rocky, Alma, and Fedora use `dnf` and `rpm`.

The package name for the same software can vary by distribution: Apache HTTP Server is usually `httpd` on the RHEL family and `apache2` on the Debian family. Identify the distribution and correct package name first.

commands.what: Shows the distribution name, version, and identifier.
commands.where: Before choosing a package command or service name.
commands.why: It confirms whether the system is in the Debian or RHEL family.

commands.what: Searches configured repositories by package name or description.
commands.where: When you are unsure of the package name.
commands.why: It reduces the chance of installing the wrong package.

sections.tip: Choose `apt` or `dnf` for the system family; do not assume the same command is available everywhere.

sections.title: Search, install, and update
body: Before installing, inspect the package description and source. `apt update` refreshes package lists on Debian-family systems; it does not upgrade packages by itself. `dnf check-update` checks whether updates are available.

Installing packages and system updates requires administrator privileges. Read the confirmation prompt to see which packages will be installed, removed, or updated. Cancel if critical, unexpected changes are listed.

commands.cmd: sudo apt install package / sudo dnf install package
commands.what: Installs a repository package and its required dependencies.
commands.where: After verifying the package name and source.
commands.why: It keeps the package database consistent instead of placing downloaded files manually.

commands.cmd: sudo apt update / sudo dnf check-update
commands.what: Refreshes repository package information or checks for updates.
commands.where: Before Debian-family installations or when checking for updates.
commands.why: The package manager uses current repository information.

sections.tip: `apt update` refreshes package lists; use `apt upgrade` separately to upgrade installed packages.

sections.title: Remove and verify packages
body: `apt remove` and `dnf remove` may affect dependencies when removing a package. `apt purge` also removes package configuration; `autoremove` finds dependencies that are no longer needed. Review the proposed removals carefully.
`dpkg -l` or `rpm -qa` lists installed packages. These lower-level tools are useful for queries, not installation; use `apt` or `dnf` to install or remove packages.

commands.cmd: sudo apt remove / sudo dnf remove
commands.what: Removes a package through the package manager.
commands.where: When a test package is no longer needed.
commands.why: It updates the package database and dependencies in a controlled way.

commands.what: Queries the list of installed packages.
commands.where: When verifying whether a package is installed.
commands.why: It reports the installation state from the package database.

sections.warn: Installing or removing packages changes the system. Practise only in your own VM; do not remove critical packages such as `kernel`, `systemd`, SSH, or networking tools. Review the confirmation list.

t01.text: Find the high-level package manager for the RHEL family in the package notes.

t02.text: Find the high-level package manager for Ubuntu/Debian.

t03.text: Predict how many lines contain `package`, then verify with `grep -c`.

t04.text: Write in `~/lab/install_plan.txt` that Ubuntu/Debian should refresh repository lists before installing.

t05.text: Add the `cowsay` installation command for both the RHEL and Debian families to your plan.

t06.text: Write a cleanup plan reminding you to review `autoremove` suggestions before removing a test package.

t07.text: For ticket #5501, note that you should identify the distribution and that the web package is named `httpd` or `apache2` depending on the family.

vm.intro: Installing and removing packages changes your system. Work only in your own test VM, never on a production system, and always read confirmation prompts.

v01.title: Identify the distribution
v01.text: Check the distribution identifier and which package tools are available.

blocks.expected: The ID= line identifies the distribution; apt or dnf is available for your family.

differs: You may not have both package managers; use the one for your distribution.
ID or ID_LIKE helps identify the distribution family.

v02.title: Inspect a package before installing
v02.text: First display information about the `cowsay` package. Run only the command appropriate for your distribution.
differs: Use apt-cache on Debian/Ubuntu and dnf on Rocky/Alma/Fedora.
If the package is not found, package lists may be stale or an enabled repository may not contain it.

v03.title: Install a test package
v03.text: Install the small `cowsay` package only in your own test VM, using the command for your distribution. Review the changes in the confirmation prompt.

blocks.expected: Setting up cowsay or installation complete

differs: Run only one block: apt for Debian/Ubuntu, dnf for the RHEL family.
If the package cannot be found, check the repository and package name before proceeding.

v04.title: Remove the test package
v04.text: After the test, remove `cowsay` with the same package manager and verify the result. Review the proposed removals before confirming.

blocks.expected: Removing cowsay or cowsay was removed

differs: Use only the command for the distribution family where you installed the package.
If unexpected important packages are listed, do not confirm; cancel with `n`.

q1.q: Which high-level package tool is commonly used on Ubuntu and Debian?
q1.explain: `apt` manages repositories and package installations on Debian-family systems.

q2.q: What is the usual Apache HTTP Server package name on the RHEL family?
q2.explain: It is usually httpd on the RHEL family and apache2 on the Debian family.

q3.explain: apt update refreshes local repository indexes; use apt upgrade to upgrade installed packages.

q4.q: What should you do at an installation confirmation prompt?
options: Press Enter without reading the output
Review packages to be added or removed
q4.explain: Dependency resolution can change other packages; review the list before proceeding.

summary: Ubuntu/Debian: apt/dpkg; Rocky/Alma/Fedora: dnf/rpm. Verify your distribution and package names first.
`apt update` refreshes package lists; installation and upgrades are separate operations.
Review proposed changes before removal and `autoremove`; protect critical system packages.

glossary.meaning: A software source where a distribution publishes packages and package information.
Another package required for a package to install or run.
A tool that installs, updates, and removes packages and their dependencies.
